full_judgment:
2. The petitioners instituted O.C. Suit No. 96 of 1971 in the 1st Court of Munsif, Kishoreganj for specific performance of contract for sale of the suit property against Sadhan Kumar Pal Chowdhury and Ranjit Kumar Pal Chowdhury. After promulgation of the P.O. 142 of 1972 the defendant-respondent, namely, Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Mymensingh was added as a proforma defendant No. 3. As the opposite party did not enter appearance to contest the suit it was decreed ex-parte by the learned Munsif on 8.2.75. Thereafter on 3.1.79 opposite party No. 3, namely, respondent instituted Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 1979 before the learned Munsif under Order 9 Rule 13 C.P.C. for setting aside the ex-parte decree on the ground that no summons was served on him. 

 3. The learned Munsif found that the summons was sought to be served by registered post on 12.12.74. But the Government pleader of Kishoreganj Court not having received any summons of the suit and he being the agent of the Government for the purpose of receiving process against the Government under Order 27 Rule 4 C.P.C. there was no proper service of summons. In that view of the matter he set aside the ex-parte decree and restored the suit to its original file and number. Thereafter the petitioner preferred Civil Revision Case No. 29 of 1982 before the District Judge, Mymensingh which was heard by the learned Additional District Judge 4th Court Mymensingh who also affirmed the judgment and order of the learned Munsif. Thereafter the petitioners moved the High Court Division and the same was also rejected.
